about: Topic map of the AP Statistics Course and Exam Description (revised, effective fall 2026), written in LevlPrep's own words from docs/apstat-research/framework.md. No CED text is reproduced. Titles: Units 1-3 read in the CED; Unit 4 and 5 titles checked against the official student course page (7 of 10 and 4 of 5 there or in the CED text) and three third-party sites that agree; each topic's source says which. Objectives and knowledge lines are summaries, not CED text, and beyond 2.1 are not text-verified (docs/apstat-needs-author.md, ced-text).

ced.title: AP Statistics Course and Exam Description
ced.edition: Revised course, effective fall 2026 (5 units, 55 topics)
ced.verification: CED PDF text readable to about 110k characters (through Unit 2 and the Course at a Glance for Unit 3 and parts of 4-5); reference sheet read in full; student course page read (2026-10-17).

skillNames.2.A: Identify the information needed to answer a question
skillNames.2.B: Justify an ethical method for gathering and representing data
skillNames.2.D: Identify types of errors and how the parts of inference relate

skillNames.3.B: Calculate summary statistics, relative positions and predicted responses
skillNames.3.C: Calculate expected counts, percentages, probabilities and intervals
skillNames.3.D: Calculate means, standard deviations and parameters of distributions
skillNames.3.E: Calculate the results of an inference method

skillNames.4.A: Describe and compare representations and summaries
skillNames.4.D: Interpret calculations to assess meaning or a claim
skillNames.4.E: Justify a method by verifying conditions
skillNames.4.G: Justify a claim from the results of inference

units.title: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: What Can We Learn from Data?
objectives: Say what question a study can answer and what population and sample it uses.
knowledge: A study answers a question about a population using data from a sample.
Results are stated in the context of the question.

topics.title: Variables
objectives: Identify observational units and classify variables; tell a parameter from a statistic.
knowledge: Variables are categorical or quantitative; quantitative ones are discrete or continuous.
A parameter describes a population; a statistic describes a sample.

topics.title: Tabular Representation and Summary Statistics for One Categorical Variable
objectives: Summarize one categorical variable with frequency and relative frequency tables.
knowledge: A relative frequency is a count divided by the total; a sample proportion is one.

topics.title: Graphical Representations for One Categorical Variable
objectives: Display and compare categorical data with bar charts and pie charts.
knowledge: Bar heights show counts or proportions; comparisons need the same scale.

topics.title: Graphical Representations for One Quantitative Variable
objectives: Display one quantitative variable with dotplots, stemplots and histograms.
knowledge: A histogram's look depends on its bin width; cumulative graphs show percentiles.

topics.title: Descriptions for One Quantitative Variable Distributions
objectives: Describe shape, center, spread and unusual features in context.
knowledge: Shapes: symmetric, skewed left or right, unimodal, bimodal, uniform.
Unusual features: outliers, gaps, clusters.

topics.title: Summary Statistics for One Quantitative Variable
objectives: Calculate and interpret mean, median, quartiles, range, IQR and standard deviation; spot outliers.
knowledge: Outlier rules: beyond 1.5 IQR from the quartiles, or more than 2 standard deviations from the mean.
Median and IQR resist outliers; mean, range and SD do not.
Changing units shifts and scales the summaries in predictable ways.

topics.title: Graphical Representations of Summary Statistics for One Quantitative Variable
objectives: Draw and read boxplots from the five-number summary, with outliers marked.
knowledge: A boxplot shows the five-number summary; it cannot show modality.

topics.title: Comparisons of the Distributions for One Quantitative Variable
objectives: Compare groups and find relative positions with percentiles and z-scores.
knowledge: A z-score is the value minus the mean, over the standard deviation.
Comparisons name which group is higher or more variable.

topics.title: The Investigative Question Revisited and Data Collection
objectives: Write a good investigative question and match it to a census, survey, experiment or observational study.
knowledge: A good question names the variable, parameter, population and kind of conclusion.
Only random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion; confounding blocks it otherwise.

topics.title: Random Sampling
objectives: Describe and carry out simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic samples.
knowledge: Sampling may be with or without replacement.
A procedure labels, generates, skips repeats and selects.

topics.title: Potential Problems with Sampling
objectives: Name the source of bias in a sampling method and its likely direction.
knowledge: Voluntary response, convenience, undercoverage, nonresponse and response bias.

topics.title: Experimental Design
objectives: Design and describe completely randomized, randomized block and matched pairs experiments.
knowledge: Comparison, random assignment, replication and control.
Blinding; a matched pairs design is a block design with two treatments.
Volunteers limit how far results generalize.

units.title: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions

topics.title: Tabular and Graphical Representations for the Distributions of Two Categorical Variables
objectives: Show two categorical variables with two-way tables, side-by-side and segmented bar charts and mosaic plots.
knowledge: Association shows when conditional distributions differ.

topics.title: Summary Statistics for Two Categorical Variables
objectives: Find joint, marginal and conditional relative frequencies and compare them.
knowledge: Conditional relative frequencies answer 'of those in a group, what share ...'.

topics.title: Estimating Probabilities Using Simulation
objectives: Estimate a probability by simulating a chance process many times.
knowledge: The estimate is the share of trials with the event; more trials give a steadier estimate.

topics.title: Introduction to Probability
objectives: Find probabilities of events from equally likely outcomes, including complements.
knowledge: A probability is the long-run relative frequency of an outcome.
P(not A) = 1 - P(A).

topics.title: Mutually Exclusive Events
objectives: Decide whether events are mutually exclusive and use the joint probability.
knowledge: Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together: P(A and B) = 0.

topics.title: Conditional Probability
objectives: Calculate and interpret conditional probabilities, including with the multiplication rule.
knowledge: P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B).

topics.title: Independent Events and Unions of Events
objectives: Check independence and find the probability of a union with the addition rule.
knowledge: Independent: P(A | B) = P(A).
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

topics.title: Introduction to Random Variables and Probability Distributions
objectives: Define a discrete random variable in context and give its probability distribution.
knowledge: Probabilities in a distribution are between 0 and 1 and add to 1.

topics.title: Parameters of Random Variables
objectives: Calculate and interpret the mean (expected value) and standard deviation of a discrete random variable.
knowledge: The mean weights each value by its probability.

topics.title: The Binomial Distribution
objectives: Recognize a binomial setting and calculate binomial probabilities, mean and standard deviation.
knowledge: Fixed n, two outcomes, constant p, independent trials.
Show the distribution, its parameters, the boundary and direction.

topics.title: The Normal Distribution
objectives: Find areas and boundary values for normal distributions; use the empirical rule.
knowledge: Standardize with z; areas under the curve are probabilities.

topics.title: Sampling Distributions and the Central Limit Theorem
objectives: Describe the sampling distribution of a statistic and what the Central Limit Theorem says about its shape.
knowledge: A statistic varies from sample to sample; its distribution has a center, spread and shape.
For large n, the sampling distribution of a sample mean is approximately normal.

topics.title: Estimators
objectives: Tell biased from unbiased estimators and relate variability to sample size.
knowledge: An unbiased estimator's sampling distribution is centered at the parameter.

topics.title: Sampling Distributions for Sample Proportions
objectives: Give the mean, standard deviation and shape of the sampling distribution of a sample proportion.
knowledge: Large counts: np and n(1 - p) at least 10; the 10% condition when sampling without replacement.

topics.title: Constructing a Confidence Interval for a Population Proportion
objectives: Construct a one-sample z interval for a proportion, checking conditions.
knowledge: statistic plus or minus critical value times standard error.

topics.title: Justifying a Claim Based on a Confidence Interval for a Population Proportion
objectives: Interpret an interval and its confidence level and use it to judge a claim.
knowledge: A level describes the method's long-run capture rate.

topics.title: Setting Up a Test for a Population Proportion
objectives: Write hypotheses about a population proportion and check the conditions for a test.
knowledge: Hypotheses are about parameters; the test's SE uses p0.

topics.title: p-Values
objectives: Interpret a p-value as a probability computed assuming the null hypothesis.
knowledge: Small p-values are evidence against the null.

topics.title: Carrying Out a Test for a Population Proportion
objectives: Carry out a one-sample z test for a proportion and state the conclusion in context.
knowledge: Compare the p-value with alpha; conclude about the alternative.

topics.title: Potential Errors When Performing Tests
objectives: Describe Type I and Type II errors and power in context and what changes them.
knowledge: P(Type I) = alpha; power rises with n and effect size.

topics.title: Sampling Distributions for the Difference Between Sample Proportions
objectives: Describe the sampling distribution of a difference of two sample proportions.
knowledge: Variances add for independent samples.

topics.title: Constructing a Confidence Interval for the Difference Between Two Population Proportions
objectives: Construct a two-sample z interval for a difference of proportions.
knowledge: Unpooled SE for intervals.

topics.title: Justifying a Claim Based on a Confidence Interval for the Difference Between Two Population Proportions
objectives: Use an interval for a difference to judge a claim, including whether 0 is plausible.
knowledge: An interval entirely above 0 is evidence the first proportion is larger.

topics.title: Setting Up a Test for the Difference Between Two Population Proportions
objectives: Write hypotheses and check conditions for a two-sample z test.
knowledge: The test's SE pools the two samples (p_c).

topics.title: Carrying Out a Test for the Difference Between Two Population Proportions
objectives: Carry out a two-sample z test and conclude in context.
knowledge: Conclusions about the difference of the true proportions.

topics.title: Setting Up a Chi-Square Test for Homogeneity or Independence
objectives: Choose homogeneity or independence, write hypotheses, compute expected counts and check conditions.
knowledge: Expected count = row total times column total over the grand total.

topics.title: Carrying Out a Chi-Square Test for Homogeneity or Independence
objectives: Calculate the chi-square statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value and conclude in context.
knowledge: df = (rows - 1)(columns - 1).

topics.title: Sampling Distributions for Sample Means
objectives: Give the mean, standard deviation and shape of the sampling distribution of a sample mean.
knowledge: sigma over the square root of n; normal population or large n.

topics.title: Constructing a Confidence Interval for a Population Mean or Population Mean Difference
objectives: Construct a one-sample t interval for a mean or a paired mean difference.
knowledge: t distributions with n - 1 degrees of freedom when sigma is unknown.

topics.title: Justifying a Claim Based on a Confidence Interval for a Population Mean or Population Mean Difference
objectives: Interpret a t interval and use it to judge a claim.
knowledge: As for proportions, in terms of a mean.
topics.source: third party (Fiveable, num8ers, OnePrep agree); not text-verified

topics.title: Setting Up a Test for a Population Mean or Population Mean Difference
objectives: Write hypotheses and check conditions for a one-sample or paired t test.
knowledge: Paired data: analyze the differences.
topics.source: official student course page (title) + third-party numbering

topics.title: Carrying Out a Test for a Population Mean or Population Mean Difference
objectives: Carry out a one-sample or paired t test and conclude in context.
knowledge: t = (x-bar - mu0) / (s / sqrt(n)).
topics.source: third party (Fiveable, num8ers, OnePrep agree); not text-verified

topics.title: Sampling Distributions for the Difference Between Two Sample Means
objectives: Describe the sampling distribution of a difference of two sample means.
knowledge: Variances add for independent samples.
topics.source: official student course page (title) + third-party numbering

topics.title: Constructing a Confidence Interval for the Difference Between Two Population Means
objectives: Construct a two-sample t interval for a difference of means.
knowledge: Unpooled SE; technology df or the conservative df.

topics.title: Justifying a Claim Based on a Confidence Interval for the Difference Between Two Population Means
objectives: Use an interval for a difference of means to judge a claim.
knowledge: Is 0 in the interval?
topics.source: official student course page (title) + third-party numbering

topics.title: Setting Up a Test for the Difference Between Two Population Means
objectives: Write hypotheses and check conditions for a two-sample t test.
knowledge: Two independent random samples or groups.
topics.source: third party (Fiveable, num8ers, OnePrep agree); not text-verified

topics.title: Carrying Out a Test for the Difference Between Two Population Means
objectives: Carry out a two-sample t test and conclude in context.
knowledge: Unpooled two-sample t.
topics.source: official student course page (title) + third-party numbering

topics.title: Graphical Representations Between Two Quantitative Variables
objectives: Make and describe scatterplots: direction, form, strength and unusual features.
knowledge: Explanatory variable on the horizontal axis.

topics.title: Correlation
objectives: Interpret the correlation r and know what it does not measure.
knowledge: r measures linear strength and direction; correlation is not causation.
topics.source: official student course page (title) + third-party numbering

topics.title: Linear Regression Models
objectives: Use a regression line to predict and interpret its slope and intercept in context; avoid extrapolation.
knowledge: y-hat = a + bx.

topics.title: Residuals
objectives: Calculate and interpret residuals and read residual plots.
knowledge: residual = actual - predicted; a pattern means a linear model is not appropriate.
topics.source: third party (Fiveable, num8ers, OnePrep agree); not text-verified

topics.title: Least-Squares Regression
objectives: Interpret the least-squares line, r squared and s, and the effect of unusual points.
knowledge: The least-squares line minimizes the sum of squared residuals.

skillsTopics.title: Fractions, Decimals and Percents
objectives: Convert between fractions, decimals and percents and find a part of a whole.
knowledge: A proportion is a part over a whole.

skillsTopics.title: Formulas, Order of Operations and Square Roots
objectives: Substitute into a formula and evaluate it in the right order, including sums and square roots.
knowledge: The summation sign adds a list of terms.

skillsTopics.title: Inequalities in Words
objectives: Translate 'at least', 'at most', 'fewer than' and 'more than' into inequalities.
knowledge: 'Fewer than 3' is X < 3, which is X <= 2 for counts.

skillsTopics.title: Factorials and Combinations
objectives: Count arrangements with factorials and choices with combinations.
knowledge: n choose k counts the ways to pick k of n.

skillsTopics.title: Lines: Slope and Intercept
objectives: Read and use the slope and intercept of a line.
knowledge: Slope is the change in y for each one-unit increase in x.

notOnReferenceSheet: pooled two-sample t (the sheet gives only the unpooled SE for means; the only pooled SE is p_c for proportions)
